questions.q: What does .map() return, and what happens to the original array?
options: A new array of the same length with every element transformed; the original array is never changed
The same array, modified in place
A single combined value, not an array
A shorter array containing only elements that passed a test
questions.explain: map() produces a brand-new array of transformed values and leaves the original array untouched.

options: Returns a new array containing only the elements where b > 0n is true, possibly shorter than the original
Transforms every element into a boolean
Removes elements from the original array in place
Returns a single boolean indicating whether any element is greater than 0n
questions.explain: filter() keeps only elements that pass the test function, returning a new (possibly shorter or empty) array.

questions.q: In balances.reduce((sum, b) => sum + b, 0n), what is the role of the 0n argument?
options: It specifies how many elements to process
It's the accumulator's starting value
It's the final return type, forcing the result to be a bigint regardless of input
It's ignored entirely by reduce()
questions.explain: The second argument to reduce() sets the initial value of the accumulator before processing the first element.

questions.q: In the chained example .filter(...).map(...).reduce(...), what is the overall effect on a list of transactions?
options: It deletes all transactions with a zero value from the original array
It keeps only transactions matching a condition, extracts one field from each, then collapses those values into a single total
It sorts the transactions by value, from lowest to highest
It converts the array of transactions into a single string
questions.explain: Filter narrows the set, map extracts the needed field, and reduce combines the extracted values into one result.

questions.q: Why do map, filter, and reduce largely replace hand-written for loops over arrays in modern JavaScript, according to this lesson?
options: map, filter, and reduce run synchronously while for loops are always asynchronous
They are required by the ECMAScript specification for all array operations
They express the same transform-select-combine operations more directly and chain together cleanly
for loops no longer work in modern JavaScript
questions.explain: These methods express common array operations (transform, select, combine) more directly than manual loop bookkeeping.
